summary.text: St. Dovmont took the Christian name Timothy, ruled Pskov and was remembered for defending the city and caring for its people.

blocks.text: St. Dovmont was a Lithuanian prince who reached Pskov as a refugee in 1265. The OCA says that he accepted baptism with the name Timothy and was soon chosen as the city’s prince. Pskov became the principal setting of his Christian life.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The received life links his public service with almsgiving, hospitality, support for churches and defense against military attacks. It credits him with a long period of cooperation with the city council and with strengthening Pskov’s defenses. His marriage joined him to a Russian princely family; his wife later became the nun St. Martha of Pskov.

blocks.text: After defending the city in 1299, he died later that year and was buried in Pskov’s Trinity cathedral. The account does not describe his death as an execution or martyrdom.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The OCA commemorates him on May 20 and records his sword and later intercession narratives. These are received hagiography.
